item.description: From a stationary low-angle camera position on sandy ground, a worker (ent_worker_main) stands behind a low three-course mortared brick wall (ent_brick_wall) where bricks are set on edge in an alternating pattern. Between 0.0s and 3.0s, a second person in a white shirt (ent_person_bg) walks behind the worker toward screen left and exits the left edge by 3.0s. Meanwhile, from 0.0s to 2.0s, ent_worker_main bends behind the wall handling bricks, lifts a red brick (ent_loose_bricks) onto the top course at 2.0s, and from 2.0s to 4.5s adjusts its position on edge alongside another loose brick with both hands. From 4.5s to 7.8s, ent_worker_main shifts focus to the adjacent loose brick on the right (screen right of the pair), sliding and aligning it on edge along the top of the wall, then lifts his hands away at 7.8s-8.2s while standing slightly upright. From 8.2s to 9.6s, ent_worker_main reaches back down with both hands to touch and readjust the left loose brick on edge until the clip ends at 9.6s. A masonry trowel (ent_trowel) remains untouched on the ground at right throughout.
item.context_result: Two loose bricks sit on edge atop the mortared courses without fresh mortar under them; the worker is still touching and adjusting the left brick when the recording cuts off at 9.6s.
item.camera_framing: Static low-angle medium-wide shot angled diagonally along the face of the low brick wall; worker's head is cropped out at the top edge for almost the entire clip.
item.uncertainty: Because no mortar is used under the bricks being placed in this top row, it is uncertain whether the worker is dry-laying bricks to check spacing/bond alignment or staging bricks along the wall prior to mortaring.

item.claim: The low brick wall exhibits the characteristic external appearance of Rat-Trap Bond Masonry, with bricks laid on edge in alternating headers and stretchers, and the worker demonstrates placing bricks on edge along the top course.
item.uncertainty: The internal hollow cavities are not visible from this low side angle, and the top bricks being adjusted in ve_01 are placed dry without mortar or guide strings.

item.uncertainty: The bricks being placed on edge in ve_01 have no mortar beneath them, so this span illustrates brick orientation and bond pattern rather than active mortared laying.

provisional_analysis.attempts: This 9.6-second clip contains a single continuous filming take (ve_01, 0.0s–9.6s) with a static camera and no camera resets. Within this single take, the worker performs three successive physical manipulation stages on the top course of bricks: first, lifting and placing a left brick on edge and adjusting it (approx. 1.8s–4.5s, claim_01, claim_02); second, sliding and aligning the adjacent right brick on edge followed by a brief hand release (approx. 4.5s–8.2s, claim_03); and third, reaching back down to readjust the left brick (8.2s–9.6s, claim_04), which is cut off by the end of the file.

The worker's head is already cropped out by the top frame edge for nearly the entire clip, EXCEPT between approximately 0.8s and 1.2s when his lower face briefly dips into the top edge as he bends down. In the background at upper left, a second person in a white shirt (ent_person_bg) walks leftward and exits the left frame edge between 0.0s and 3.0s (claim_05). Rather than applying a heavy zoom or crop that would sacrifice the wide perspective of the staggered brick courses, the background walker and brief face intrusion can be avoided temporally by entering the shot at or after 3.0s.
